precepts.why:
“O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty. Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind”.

The Most High makes the clouds His chariot and walks upon the wings of the wind. So the wheels Ezekiel saw by the living creatures, the wheel in the middle of a wheel, are chariots, and this answers who rides in them: the spirit riding in the chariot is the Lord. “Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went”, for “the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.”

precepts.text: The cherubims are the angels attached to the wheels, described in the vision of chapter one.
precepts.point: The vision went up from Ezekiel, and he spoke unto the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him.

note.label: Ezekiel 11: This City Shall Not Be Your Cauldron

precepts.why:
The cherubims that lift up their wings here, with the wheels beside them, are the same living creatures Ezekiel saw at the first. Back in chapter one he beheld “one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures, with his four faces”, their appearance “like unto the colour of a beryl”, and “a wheel in the middle of a wheel.” Their rings “were so high that they were dreadful”, and “full of eyes round about them four.”

The cherubims are the angels attached to the wheels. “when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.” Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, “for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” When those went, these went; when those stood, these stood.

So when the cherubims lift up their wings and the wheels lift with them, and the glory of the God of Israel is over them above, it is that same vision moving. The glory of the Lord goes up from the midst of the city and stands upon the mountain on the east side, and the spirit then takes Ezekiel in a vision into Chaldea, to them of the captivity, where he speaks to the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
All four have the face of a man, a lion on the right, an ox on the left and an eagle. Their wings stretch upward, two joined to one another and two covering their bodies. Ezekiel is describing the same beasts John sees.

Ezekiel gives the four faces together; John's lion, calf, man and eagle identify the face that dominates the front of each creature. Their appearance, eyes and wings are far beyond anything we normally encounter. Seeing such a creature would make a person fear, lose bodily control and feel his spirit leave him. Do not assume God's creation is limited to the familiar animals around us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
The clouds are the chariots the angels travel in; Ezekiel 1 talks about the wheel. “The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl:” Beryl is green. “and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.” So this chariot was like a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

“When they went, they went upon their four sides: and they turned not when they went.” When you are in a car and you want to turn, you have to make that turn. The chariots don't do that. When they want to go left they go like that, when they want to go right they go like that; they don't have to roll like a car does.

“As for their rings, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their rings were full of eyes round about them four. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.”

“Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went, thither was their spirit to go;” Imagine this. In the Black Panther movie, when she was flying that chariot, it was with her mind; they got that from this. Wherever the spirit of the angels wanted to go, that is where they went. They didn't have to think about it and make a turn. Wherever the thought was to go, that is how these chariots roll. “and the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” So the spirit and the chariot were connected; it was one. When the angel got in, the spirit connected with that vehicle and they became one.

“When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” So the spirit of the angels was in the chariot. It is hard to comprehend because we are men, but that is what it is making reference to.
